transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

...My family and friends. They made me come. 

They keep waving these bank papers in my face, trying to say it proves nothing was taken. But... I mean, it's been over a year. I've known for over a year that they're hiding my money. They just use all this stuff—like bills, or some fundraiser, or trip plans—just
For how long have you believed that people are hiding your money?
Like I said... over a year. I guess it's been about a year and two months. Just... ever since my income dropped.
During this time, have you had a period where your mood felt unusually high or irritable?
No. I just... I feel normal. I mean, I get mad when they lie to me about the money, but... no. Not like that.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
No. I don't... hear things like that. Just... no.
Has anyone done something to your body or mind that you believe would be impossible for most people to do?
No. I don't... I don't know what you're talking about. Nobody did anything to my body or my mind. Just... no.
Has anyone told you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem mixed up?
No. People understand me fine. I just... I talk normal. Nobody says anything like that.
Aside from this issue about your money, has your ability to work or manage daily life gotten a lot worse?

No. I mean... except for the arguments about the money, I do fine. I still handle my own meals. I get to the county clinic... and my assistance appointments. Keep my things in order. Just... the same way I always have. So, no.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a single, persistent persecutory/theft-related delusional belief that others are hiding or taking money for about 14 months. There is no evidence of hallucinations, bizarre passivity phenomena, disorganized speech/thought, manic episode, or marked functional deterioration outside the delusional theme, supporting persistent delusional disorder.
